data.name: Moonstone Tavern - A Fantasy Tavern Sim!
data.detailed_description:
With the death of your eccentric aunt, you have been left the once famous Moonstone Tavern. Unfortunately the tavern has seen better days. With only two functioning rooms, crumbling architecture, and an ever-diminishing reputation there is plenty of room for improvement.

Can you turn this dilapidated ruin into a thriving business? In a fantasy world filled with cunning wizards, tricky elves, cat obsessed gnomes, grumpy dwarves, and sad fairies it certainly isn’t going to be easy, especially if you want them all to stay happy under one roof. If you are going to make a go of it there is a lot to do: staff to hire, meals to cook, ingredients to forage, quests to undertake, and gods to appease. Yet if you can survive the brutal world that surrounds you there is definitely a profit to be made!

FEATURES:

• Repair, renovate, and decorate the dilapidated tavern.
• Build specialist rooms for humans, elves, fairies, gnomes, orcs, and dwarves.
• Build undersea 'beds' for the Merfolk!
• Hire cooks, priests, foragers, and heroes to help improve your tavern.
• Forage hundreds of real world items.
• Craft hundreds of items including weapons, armours, potions, scrolls, and genetimage equipment.
• Collect and breed over 50 colletable creatures to keep as pets.
• Find and ride the mystical, pink unipony!
• Interact with hundreds of unique guests with stories, rumours, and suggestions for your tavern!
• Assemble a team of heroes and mages to help you on adventures.
• Choose from 10 starting characters and from six different fantasy class types including druid, witch hunter, and gunlord.
• An involved weapon and magic system with wands, swords, guns, and spells!
• Settle into your new life by getting married and having a child.
• Invest in the local Arena - watch battles and bet on fights.
• Dynamic seasons with day and night system.
• Undertake quests to improve your tavern’s renown, find paintings to hang and specialist food to serve. Raid the castles of dark mages for supplies, loot dragon hordes for gold, and seek out lost shrines to please the gods.
• Explore a handcrafted world and visit the undercity of the gnomes, a bustling human port, and the dark village of the elves.
• Choose a god to worship and gain special powers and bonuses for your tavern.
• Take part in a non-compulsory, rpg storyline that will place you and your tavern at the centre of a plague, and amidst a magical war that threatens to overcome the three kingdoms!

reviews.review:
Moonstone Tavern: A Fantasy Tavern Sim is an engaging hybrid of tavern management, role-playing, crafting, and exploration that invites players to restore a neglected inn to its former prestige. Developed and published by Trevor Jones, the game revolves around inheriting the rundown Moonstone Tavern from a quirky relative and transforming it into a thriving destination for travelers, adventurers, and townsfolk. Rather than limiting itself to business management alone, the experience expands into a fantasy adventure where nearly every activity contributes to the tavern's long-term success. This combination of genres gives the game a distinctive identity, offering players far more than the typical management simulator.

At its core, the game revolves around rebuilding and expanding the tavern through careful planning and resource management. Players begin with only a small, deteriorating establishment that requires extensive repairs and upgrades before it can attract larger crowds. Profits earned from renting rooms, serving guests, and improving customer satisfaction can be reinvested into expanding the building, decorating interiors, and unlocking new amenities. Watching the humble tavern gradually evolve into a bustling business delivers a satisfying sense of progression that rewards patience and thoughtful decision-making.

Outside the tavern walls lies a fantasy world filled with opportunities for adventure. Players venture into forests, caves, and dangerous regions to collect crafting materials, battle monsters, complete quests, and uncover hidden treasures. These expeditions are not isolated side activities but an essential part of the overall gameplay loop, as the resources gathered during exploration directly support the tavern's development. Valuable loot can be sold, rare ingredients can be crafted into useful items, and discoveries often open new paths for expanding both the business and the player's capabilities.

Crafting is another major pillar of the experience, allowing players to produce furniture, equipment, tools, and supplies instead of relying solely on merchants. Harvesting resources and creating useful items strengthens the feeling of self-sufficiency while adding another rewarding layer to progression. The interconnected nature of exploration, gathering, crafting, and management ensures that no activity feels disconnected from the others. Every expedition contributes to the tavern, and every improvement to the tavern provides greater opportunities for future adventures.

The game's retro-inspired pixel art complements its fantasy setting with a warm and nostalgic atmosphere. Character sprites, environments, and interior designs evoke the charm of classic role-playing games while maintaining a cozy aesthetic that suits the relaxed pace of tavern life. Although the visuals are relatively simple compared to modern simulation titles, they possess enough personality to make the world inviting. Combined with pleasant music and ambient sound effects, the presentation encourages players to settle into the steady rhythm of building a successful establishment.

One of the game's greatest strengths is the freedom it gives players to determine how they wish to progress. Some may dedicate their efforts to maximizing tavern efficiency and attracting more guests, while others may spend extended periods exploring the wilderness in search of rare materials and valuable treasures. The absence of a rigid progression system makes each playthrough feel more personal, allowing players to prioritize the aspects they enjoy most while gradually unlocking additional content.

Despite its creative design, Moonstone Tavern is not without flaws. The user interface occasionally feels cumbersome, and certain mechanics could benefit from clearer tutorials or better explanations. Inventory management sometimes becomes tedious, while the pacing of gathering resources may feel repetitive during longer sessions. Combat and exploration, although enjoyable, can also become somewhat predictable as players encounter familiar enemies and repeated tasks. These rough edges reveal the limitations of an ambitious independent project, even though they rarely overshadow the core gameplay loop.

Overall, Moonstone Tavern: A Fantasy Tavern Sim successfully blends business management with fantasy role-playing to create a relaxing and rewarding experience for players who enjoy gradual progression and open-ended gameplay. Its combination of tavern customization, exploration, crafting, and character growth offers plenty of variety, ensuring that players are rarely confined to a single activity for long. While the game lacks the refinement and polish of larger-budget simulators, its creativity, charm, and interconnected systems make it a worthwhile experience for fans of fantasy management games and sandbox RPGs alike.

Rating: 5/10
